title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults & uecon tooling for batching/caching/quant
author: Diego Chen
release_notes: Improved autotuning defaults for batching/caching and added unit-economics tooling; safe defaults are backward compatible and can be overridden via config. Includes minor docs and CLI UX updates.
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common workloads by shipping safer autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduce tuned quantization profiles for common model classes, and add initial unit-economics (uecon) tooling so SREs and platform owners can see estimated $/1000 tokens and projected cost savings. This PR consolidates several initiatives (ENG-3245, ENG-3301, PM-112) into a single merge to simplify rollout.
commits: feat(autotune): add defaults for min/max batch sizes and cache thresholds
perf(batching): introduce dynamic batch window estimator based on 95th pct latency
feat(quant): add 'recommended' quant profiles (int8/4bit-mixed) and selection heuristics
feat(uecon): initial CLI + console hooks for unit-economics estimation
test: add integration tests for batching + caching behavior under synthetic workloads
docs: cost-optimization guides and migration notes
review_comments: Ava Martin: Overall this looks good. Two requests: (1) make the default batch max configurable per-deployment via helm values, and (2) add a safety guard to prevent batch growth during cold-start spikes.
Diego Chen: Addressed both comments in commits 3 and 4; helm value is helm/values-autotune.yaml.autotune.batch_max and we now cap growth rate to 2x per minute, with telemetry to detect oscillation.
Rina Patel: Can we add a short note in docs about interaction between prefix cache TTL and model kv-cache sizes? Observability folks will want that.
Diego Chen: Added section 'Cache interactions' to docs/cost-optimization.md and added a console tooltip with the same guidance.
Samuel Ortiz: Found flaky test in integration run (autotune_bench_test.go), failing under simulated high QPS. Suggested adding deterministic seed and lowering parallelism in test harness.
Diego Chen: Fixed test harness seed and reduced test concurrency; reran CI and all checks passed (see CI summary).
